resolutionReport.command: python3.12 -m pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --only-binary=:all: --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_31_x86_64 --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 --platform linux_x86_64 --python-version 3.11 --implementation cp --abi cp311 --abi abi3 --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 'vllm @ https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/v0.30.0/vllm-0.30.0%2Bcu129-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl'

evidenceGaps: NOT a promotion lock. Generated by resolving the pinned cu129 release wheel with `pip install --dry-run --report` on a macOS arm64 host using explicit --platform manylinux_2_17/2_28/2_31_x86_64, linux_x86_64 and --python-version 3.11. The Kaggle base image Python minor version is still unknown, so the cp311 torch-stack hashes below are NOT proven to be the ones the target image installs.

Only the cp311 linux-x86_64 variants are captured. The registry allows CPython 3.10-3.14, and torch/torchvision/torchaudio publish a different wheel per CPython, so a cp310/cp312/cp313/cp314 image needs its own resolution before this closure can be locked.
flashinfer-cubin 0.6.18.post1 is not on PyPI (https://flashinfer.ai/whl/) and did not appear in this resolution; whether the frozen runtime needs it is still undecided.

The pytorch cu129 index publishes torch and torchaudio wheels with a #sha256 fragment, but publishes torchvision 0.28.0+cu129 and Jinja2 WITHOUT one. The two hashes marked localDigest below were computed by downloading those exact wheel URLs and hashing them; they are not independently corroborated by a second source.
torchaudio 2.11.0 declares no torch dependency, so torchaudio/torch skew is only detectable by import inside the venv; no target-image import smoke has run.
